why.title: A community that passes on, acts and helps out.
why.lead: Three things you won’t find together anywhere else: verified mentors who save you months, community projects that change real people’s lives, and testers for your app before it ships.
why.mentorTitle: A mentor to get you unstuck, for free
why.mentorText: Stuck on a precise problem? An experienced developer, verified by KABAD, helps you solve it on a video call. You pick your mentor, book a slot in their calendar and describe your problem. The session lasts 30 min to 1 h, it is free, and you leave unstuck.
why.mentorProblem: “My mobile money payment fails one time out of three.”
why.mentorSessionText: Thursday at 3 pm, on Google Meet
why.riseText: Start or join community projects: developers from all over Africa contribute to move sectors like fintech, farming or health forward, or to create unique, practical innovations. African talent transforms local communities there, and these projects can be showcased worldwide.
why.project1: Tracking drinking-water boreholes in the Sahel
why.testsTitle: Get your app tested before you ship it
why.testsText: Alone, you can’t see every bug in your own app, and finding real testers is hard. On KABAD, you post a listing with the tasks to check. Devs from the community test your app on their own phones and send you clear feedback, with screenshots. You fix things before your users hit the problem.
why.test1: You post your listing and the tasks to test
why.test2: A group of testers forms around your app
why.test3: Everyone tests on their phone, task by task
why.test4: You get clear feedback, with screenshots

features.title: Everything you need to grow, in one app.
features.lead: A web app you can install on your phone, designed mobile first. Pick a feature to see it.
features.label: Features
features.mentoringText: Free sessions of 30 min to 1 h with verified mentors. You book a slot like in a calendar, the mentor accepts, the video call is ready.
features.hackathonsText: Online, on site or hybrid. Take part solo or as a team, join a team looking for your profile, and KABAD instructors prepare the teams.
features.testsText: Post a listing, say what to test, and a group of testers sends back structured feedback, with screenshots.
features.messagingText: Invitations, conversations and themed groups. Text, audio, images and files, to move forward together between sessions.
features.riseText: Project channels by African challenge, live rooms and events, to build solutions that matter.

how.title: Three steps to join the community.
how.lead: No application, no waiting list. An account, a profile, and the community opens up.
how.s1Text: An e-mail, a password, and you confirm your address with the code you receive.
how.s2Text: Your country, your level, your tech, and what you’re here for: a mentor, hackathons, testers, Rise-Up projects.
how.s3Text: We suggest devs to meet as soon as you sign up. And if you have experience, ask for your mentor badge: KABAD validates it.

vision.quote: Create the next generation of African developers, more productive and more skilled in the age of AI.
vision.text: And through them, solve real problems in Africa, then showcase these solutions worldwide. A project born at the African Developers Cup, built by devs, for devs.
vision.illustration: An African developer raises a trophy, as a winner
vision.p1Text: Mentoring, hackathons, mutual help and community feedback on their apps.
vision.p2Text: Water, health, farming, education, energy, finance: African challenges, local solutions.
vision.p3Text: Solutions born on KABAD are made to be shown, carried and reused elsewhere.

organize.title: Running a hackathon? Launch it on KABAD.
organize.text: For your company, your incubator, your community or your school: create your hackathon from your KABAD account, online, on site or hybrid, and recruit KABAD mentors as instructors to prepare the teams.
organize.p1: A challenge, rules, prizes: you set the frame
organize.p2: Verified KABAD instructors, paid per mission
organize.p3: Registrations, teams and submissions handled in the app
organize.p4: Participants from the whole continent and the diaspora

faq.title: What we’re asked the most.
faq.a1: Yes. The account, mentoring, taking part in hackathons, app testing and Rise-Up projects are free for devs. Only the dev who runs a hackathon and recruits instructors pays for their mission.
faq.a2: A dev with at least three years of experience, who describes their expertise and shares a link to their work (GitHub, LinkedIn or portfolio). The KABAD team reviews every request and grants the badge, or explains why it declines.
faq.q3: How does a mentoring session work?
faq.a3: You pick a slot in the mentor’s calendar and describe your problem. A session lasts 30 min to 1 h: slots are 30 minutes long, and you can book two in a row. The mentor accepts, and you both get a Google Meet link. No messages to exchange before, no commitment after.
faq.q4: Do I need to install an app?
faq.a4: KABAD is a web app: it opens in your browser and installs on your phone in one gesture, without going through an app store. It also works on tablet and computer.
faq.q5: I live in the diaspora, is it for me?
faq.a5: Yes, it’s even one of the starting points of the project: connecting devs on the continent with those living elsewhere, so experience flows both ways.

final.title: Join the first devs on KABAD.
final.text: An account, an e-mail, and you get mentoring, hackathons and Rise-Up projects. Have experience to share? Ask for your mentor badge, KABAD validates it.
